Recognitions filled the opening: the 2025-2026 high school student representatives, spring 2025 all-state athletes, an all-girls robotics team named Global Team of the Year, and ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the year ending June 30, 2024. The most consequential action was unanimous acceptance of the administration's Attendance Area Review recommendation, approving boundary modifications effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 16, 2025, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart; adjourned at 9:34 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary.

**Attendance**
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler; Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Griffor, Trudel, and Milanov. Approximately 100 members of the audience. Every recorded vote was Yes 7, No 0.

**Recognitions**
- 2025-2026 student representatives: Chloe Gentilini (Troy College & Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), Sara Graunstadt (Athens High School), Isabella "Bella" Doss (Troy High School).
- Spring 2025 all-state athletes: Ashley Miller, Lauren DeJonckheere, Julian Farrell, Myles Linden, Katie Malon (Athens); Chase Duncan, Jason Hamilton, Olivia Jasniewicz (Troy High).
- Mission Moment: the district's first all-girls robotics team, founded December 2022, named Global Team of the Year; Coach Judy Bunao introduced the team.
- Student Spotlight: Creative Guild podcasters Sohyeon An (Smith) and Sidthbhiphob Suriwong (Larson), presented by Thomas Butcher.
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, credited to Dan Trudel, Aurel Malutan, and the Finance Team.

**Proclamation**
At the request of Oakland Community Health Network, the Board adopted a proclamation recognizing September 2025 as National Suicide Prevention Month (Anne / Alic). It cites World Suicide Prevention Day on September 10, the CDC figure of more than 48,000 deaths by suicide each year, and suicide as the second leading cause of death for people 10 to 34 years of age. Adopted 7-0.

**Consent Agenda and Personnel**
Items A and B approved (Haupt / Alic): minutes of the August 19, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting and the Treasurer's Report for July 2025. John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on hiring drivers - retirements/resignations, leaves of absence, FTE status, enrollment - and noted the District hired 31 new teachers this year. Personnel recommendations approved (Alic / Anne). Curriculum: none.

**Business Actions**

| Item | Amount | Fund | Motion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Administration Building renovation | $1,560,680.30 | Capital Projects Fund | Haupt / Alic |
| Entrance ceiling soffits | $373,127.00 | Building Site and Sinking Fund | Haupt / Anne |
| Operable partition walls, Hamilton and Wass - Gardiner Vose, Inc. | $111,955.00 | Building Site and Sinking Fund | Anne / Haupt |

Dan Trudel gave a Bond Showcase Report with a PowerPoint of project photographs and statuses, covering Athens High School, Boulan Park Middle School, and elementary updates.

**Other Business**
- MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly, October 23 at 7:00 p.m.: Emina Alic, Audra Melton, Stephanie Zendler certified as delegates; Ayesha Potts alternate (Alic / Anne).
- 2026 NSBA Advocacy Institute, Washington, D.C., February 1-3, 2026: no more than two Board members (Potts / Haupt).
- 2026 NSBA Annual Conference for Public Education Leaders, San Antonio, Texas, April 10-12, 2026: no more than four Board members (Melton / Zendler).
- Attendance Area Review: Dr. Machesky presented the AARC recommendation; the Board approved the modifications effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year (Melton / Haupt).

**Public Comment and Announcements**
One community member spoke on agenda items and one on non-agenda items; no action taken. The student representatives reported on school activities. Board comment topics: the cell phone policy, the Oakland County Government Relations Network Meeting, bond funds, the MASA Conference, the BOE Community Conversation on September 25 at 5:30 pm, no state budget yet, National School Attendance Month, TYA Magic of Hope, and the September 24 Business Roundtable. Next Board Workshop: October 7 at 6:00 p.m.; next regular meeting: October 14 at 7:00 p.m., Services Building.
2025_082_m091625bdmtg.verbose:
**Document and setting**
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held September 16, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present, along with Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Griffor, Trudel, and Milanov. Approximately 100 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:34 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary (EA/jh).

**Student representatives to the Board, 2025-2026**
Chloe Gentilini, Troy College & Career High School: senior, student council and prom committee member, school store staff member, varsity student athlete, and a leader of Women of the Tomorrow; involved in Adopt a Family and Operation Blue Slay.
Ahyoung Song, International Academy-East: junior pursuing an IB diploma; captain of Science Olympiad, co-president of Science Fair, president of the Southeast and East Asian Student Association; leads the districtwide Math Pentathlon program across 3 elementary schools, coaching over 100 students at Costello and Hamilton Elementary schools; has presented research at the Michigan Science Fair and the International Science and Engineering Fair.
Sara Graunstadt, Athens High School: senior, Drum Major of the Athens Marching Band and flute player, member of the three-time state champion Athens powerlifting team; plans a career in pediatric speech-language pathology.
Isabella "Bella" Doss, Troy High School: senior, Vice President of the Student Government and Leadership Executive Board, Communications Director on the Troy High Model UN Executive Board, member of DECA and LEAP, representative of Troy High and Oakland County in the Michigan Association of Student Councils and Honor Societies (MASC/MAHS), and Chair of the Board's DEI Committee; spent two years on the Troy High School Drumline; plans to study business on the pre-law track.

**All-State Athletes - 2025 Spring Sports**
Mr. Jansen and the Board recognized: Ashley Miller, senior, Athens, girls' soccer; Lauren DeJonckheere, senior, Athens, girls' soccer; Julian Farrell, senior, Athens, boys' track; Myles Linden, senior, Athens, boys' track; Katie Malon, junior, Athens, girls' lacrosse; Chase Duncan, senior, Troy High, girls' lacrosse; Jason Hamilton, senior, Troy High, boys' track; Olivia Jasniewicz, junior, Troy High, girls' soccer.

**Mission Moment: all-girls robotics team, Global Team of the Year**
The Board featured the district's first all-girls robotics team as the September Mission Moment. Founded in December 2022, the team was named Global Team of the Year at an international tournament where it also led a global workshop. Coach Judy Bunao introduced the team. 2025-2026 season members: Jianna Cruz, Haneul Kim, Varna Jayaraman, Merrill Sanchez, Aarohi Sonar, Keerthana Chandra, Anwitha Vemuri. Youth mentors: Ella Bunao, Christel Jebu Mathew, Emmelyn Lauder, Gargi Sonawane, Sophia Alexander, Lauren Sanchez. Coaches and founders: Judy Bunao (Founder & Coach), Ed Bunao (Founder & Coach), Varun Jayaraman (Coach).

**Student Spotlight**
The first Student Spotlight of the year recognized Creative Guild students Sohyeon An, an 8th grader at Smith, and Sidthbhiphob Suriwong, an 8th grader at Larson, collaborators on a podcast project. Thomas Butcher shared their accomplishments.

**National Suicide Prevention Month proclamation**
Oakland Community Health Network (OCHN) asked school boards throughout Oakland County to approve a proclamation for September as National Suicide Prevention Month. Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Alic. The whereas clauses note that World Suicide Prevention Day is observed each year on September 10; that suicidal thoughts can affect anyone regardless of age, gender, race, orientation, income level, religion, or background; that according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) each year more than 48,000 people died by suicide; that suicide is the second leading cause of death for people 10 to 34 years of age, the fourth leading cause among people 35 to 54 years of age, and the eighth leading cause among people 55 to 64 years of age; that the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) and the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, 988, help individuals in crisis; and that OCHN is committed to being a Zero Suicide organization. The resolution has OCHN recognize September 2025 as National Suicide Prevention Month and calls upon government agencies, public and private institutions, businesses, faith-based organizations, and schools to increase awareness of suicide prevention. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution adopted.

**ASBO Excellence in Financial Reporting for FY2024**
Dr. Philippart recognized the Business Office team for again receiving the ASBO Award. The Association of School Business Officials (ASBO) International awarded the Troy School District its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, for a high-quality Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR). Credited were Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Dan Trudel, Finance Director Aurel Malutan, and the TSD Finance Team.

**Additions and deletions; public communication**
Additions and deletions: none. One community member addressed the Board on agenda items; no action was taken.

**Consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, the Board approved items A and B: minutes of the August 19, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting, and the Treasurer's Report - July 2025. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Personnel - staffing update and new hires**
John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the District's hiring process and the factors influencing the number of teachers hired each year, including retirements/resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status, and student enrollment. This year the District hired 31 new teachers.
Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board approved the personnel recommendations. New hires: Heraldo Henrique Anjos Hatton, Caryn Baird, Alexandra Balcoff, Shawn Boucke, Julia Choi, Emily Conley, Dillon Coulter, Amy Dzapo, Bailey Fahnestock, Kenedi Harmon, Emma Hauberg, Erika Head, Jennifer Holdstock, Olivia Horrigan, Michael Jennings, Colin Johnson, Erica Johnson-Veggian, Crissy Karaszewski, Amanda Kovacs, Jennifer Liddell, Jessica Lovelace, Amy Macintosh, Mackenzie Maher, Grace Merriman, Abigail Minor, Neal Mozdzierz, Delaney O'Dell, Timothy Paccione, Shreya Patel, Julia Plesz, Erin Prendergast, Tex Profitt, Dana Reimann, Zoe Rosario, Jason Rose, Lauren Rouff, Kylie Schmehl, Tara Sheridan, Victoria Smirnov, Luke Telder, Heather Temrowski, Allison Van Buhler, Adrienne Weston, Anna Wilner. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Curriculum**
None.

**Business - construction and facilities bids**
Administration Building Renovation: moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, the bid was awarded as attached in the amount of $1,560,680.30, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund, with the renovation awarded to the vendors listed in the attachment. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
Elementary Soffit Replacement Project: moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Anne, the bid for the purchase and installation of entrance ceiling soffits was awarded as attached in the amount of $373,127.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
Hamilton & Wass Operable Wall Replacement: moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mr. Haupt, the bid for operable partition walls for Hamilton and Wass Elementaries was awarded to Gardiner Vose, Inc. in the amount of $111,955.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Bond Showcase Report**
Assistant Superintendent Dan Trudel gave a brief report updating the Board and community on bond projects throughout the District, sharing a PowerPoint presentation with photographs and the status of each project. He discussed upcoming projects and construction of Athens High School, Boulan Park Middle School, and elementary updates.

**Public communication (non-agenda items) and student reports**
One community member addressed the Board; no action was taken. Chloe Gentilini, Ahyoung Song, Sara Graunstadt, and Isabella (Bella) Doss each reported on events and activities at their schools.

**Other - conference and assembly representation**
MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly: moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board certified Emina Alic, Audra Melton, and Stephanie Zendler as delegates to the MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly on October 23 at 7:00 p.m., with Ayesha Potts as alternate. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
NSBA Advocacy Institute 2026, Washington, D.C., February 1 - 3, 2026: moved by Mrs. Potts, supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board approved a delegation of no more than two (2) Board members. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
NSBA 2026 Annual Conference for Public Education Leaders, San Antonio, Texas, April 10 - 12, 2026: moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mrs. Zendler, the Board approved a delegation of no more than four (4) Board members. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**AARC recommendation and acceptance**
Dr. Machesky shared administration's recommendation for the Attendance Area Review project, with a brief history of the AARC process and the reasoning behind it. Moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mr. Haupt, the resolution recites the need for periodic review of attendance areas to maintain balanced enrollment, maximize effective use of district facilities, and support students' academic, social, and emotional needs, and the administration's analysis of enrollment data, projected student population trends, and facility capacities, plus stakeholder engagement through public meetings, surveys, and other outreach. The Board approved the recommended modifications as provided, effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year, and directed the Superintendent and administrative team to implement the changes as presented. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Board comments and announcements**
Board members welcomed new staff and everyone back to the new school year, mentioning: the cell phone policy and restrictions in schools; the Oakland County Government Relations Network Meeting; bond funds; the MASA Conference; the BOE Community Conversation on September 25 at 5:30 pm; fall updates to building staff and PTOs beginning in October; curriculum nights; no state budget yet, with the community urged to write to legislators; National School Attendance Month; TYA Magic of Hope; and the Business Roundtable on September 24th. Dr. Philippart announced the next Board Workshop in the Administration Building on October 7th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting on October 14th in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m.
